key_insight: PROUD reduces forgetting in multimodal continual instruction tuning by constraining updates to an optimized low-rank subspace in the vision-language projector’s final linear layer.
engineering_relevance: This is an AI adaptation method, not a constitutive modeling study; its potential engineering value is updating multimodal assistants without adding inference or routing overhead.
method: Combine retained input statistics and initial task gradients to select a metric-orthonormal update subspace.
Maximize first-order task gain under a drift budget, then regularize updates with an exact Frobenius penalty.
Merge the learned updates into the terminal projector layer without additional inference modules.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved continual accuracy and reduced forgetting versus recent replay-free baselines on UCIT and CoIN across MLLM backbones, using fewer trainable parameters, but gives no numerical results.
watch_item: A fixed subspace selected at task onset may limit adaptation as task gradients evolve; solid-mechanics performance is not evaluated in the abstract.
paper_title: Projector Subspace Optimization for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
